Since \(n \mid 3^n\), \(n\) must be a power of \(3\), say \(n=3^k\).

Then the second condition is
\[
3^k-1 \mid 3^{3^k}-1.
\]
This holds iff \(k \mid 3^k\), so \(k\) must also be a power of \(3\). Thus the first two possibilities are
\[
k=1 \Rightarrow n=3,\qquad k=3 \Rightarrow n=27.
\]
Their sum is \(3+27=30\).

\[
\boxed{30}
\]
